question_text: Attempt either option A or B. A. During artificial hybridization, it is important to ensure that only desired pollen grains are used for pollination. How is it ensured? OR B. Why is manual transfer of desired pollen grains relatively easy in pea plants for hybridization, but in wheat, pollen grains are often utilized from pollen banks for hybridization purposes?
answer_text: A. Emasculate the bisexual flower before anther dehiscence and bag it; when the stigma is receptive, dust desired pollen and rebag. OR B. Pea has large, easily handled flowers and viable pollen can be transferred immediately; wheat pollen is short-lived and difficult to handle, so stored pollen from pollen banks is useful.
answer_explanation: Emasculation and bagging prevent unwanted pollination.

question_text: How is the rate of initiatio n of RNA polymerase at a given promoter in a transcriptional unit of prokaryotes regulated?
answer_text: Regulatory proteins bind to the operator/promoter region and alter RNA polymerase access. Repressors reduce initiation, while activators increase the frequency with which RNA polymerase binds and begins transcription.
answer_explanation: Prokaryotic transcription is chiefly controlled at initiation.

question_text: Attempt either option A or B. A. A cheese maker claims to be a biotechnologist. How will you support the same? OR B. Why does the 'insertional inactivation' method to detect recombinant DNA is preferred to 'antibiotic resistance' procedure?

question_text: Attempt either option A or B. A. (i) Compare the two ecological pyramids of biomass I and II given below and explain the situations in which this is possible. A tropical rainforest in South America is home to more than 40,000 species of plants, 3,000 of fishes, 1,300 of birds, 427 of mammals, 427 of amphibians, 378 of reptiles and 1,25,000 insects, snails and worms. From the given data, calculate the total num ber of known vertebrate species in the rainforest. (i) Give a reason to justify the huge difference in the number of plant and animal species. . Section - C
answer_text: A(i) Biomass pyramid is upright in terrestrial ecosystems but may be inverted in aquatic ecosystems because phytoplankton have low standing biomass yet high turnover. (ii) From 200,000 J sunlight, producers trap about 2,000 J; primary consumers receive ~200 J, secondary 20 J, tertiary 2 J. OR B total known vertebrates=3000+1300+427+427+378=5532; tropical stability, high productivity and long evolutionary time favour greater diversity.
answer_explanation: Energy transfer follows the 10% law after producers capture a small fraction of sunlight.

question_text: Suggest a suitable contraceptive device for the following cases with justification. (i) Mohini does not want to t ake the risk of conception and sexually transmitted infections (STIs). (ii) Lalita has two children and does not want any more children. (iii) Geeta wants a contraceptive that she can take till she wants to avoid conception and can resume back to her fertile life without the intervention of the doctor. Also, it should have a lower failure rate.
answer_text: (i) Condom: prevents conception and reduces STI transmission. (ii) Tubectomy: permanent method after completing family. (iii) Oral contraceptive pills: reversible, user-controlled and low failure rate when taken correctly.
answer_explanation: The method must match STI protection, permanence and reversibility needs.

question_text: Given below is a figure showing transport of ovum, fertilisation and passage of growing embryo through fallopian tube in a human female. Answer the questions that follow: (i) What will be the ploidy of cells shown in (a) and (c) stage in the figure given below? (ii) What will happen if component L as shown in the figure (g) given below does not attach properly to the endometrium? (iii) In a pregnant mother (case X), during early pregnancy, the fertilised egg splits into two embryos at stage C shown in the figure given below, resulting in the formation of twins. Will the genome of cells of these two embryos exhibit variation? Justify your answer. - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - For Visually impaired students Explain the events and journey of an ovum in the fallopian tube of a mother from fertilisation stage to implantation.
answer_text: (i) Ovum is haploid (n); post-fertilisation embryo/blastomeres are diploid (2n). (ii) If the blastocyst/trophoblast does not attach properly, implantation fails and pregnancy cannot continue. (iii) The twins are monozygotic and have essentially identical genomes because they arise by splitting of one zygote.
answer_explanation: Fertilisation restores diploidy, and implantation is essential for continued development.

question_text: In guinea pigs, black coat colour (G) dominates over white (g) and brown eyes (B) dominate over blue (b). The alleles for coat colour and eye colour are not linked. What will be the probability of the offspring having blue eyes and a white coat if both par ents are heterozygous for eye and coat colour? Find the probability using a Punnett square .
answer_text: Cross GgBb×GgBb. Probability of white coat gg=1/4; blue eyes bb=1/4. Independent assortment gives P(ggbb)=1/4×1/4=1/16 (6.25%).
answer_explanation: Unlinked genes assort independently, so probabilities multiply.

question_text: The Biological Oxygen Demand (BOD) of a primary effluent during sewage treatment is reduced. Enlist the process of how this is achieved.
answer_text: Primary effluent enters aeration tanks, where air is pumped and aerobic microbes form flocs. They oxidise organic matter, reducing BOD. The flocs settle as activated sludge; part is recycled and the rest enters anaerobic digesters.
answer_explanation: Microbial oxidation removes dissolved organic load.

question_text: Expand ELISA. On what principle is the ELISA test based? List two ways by which an infection can be detected by this test.
answer_text: ELISA means Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay. It is based on specific antigen-antibody interaction detected through an enzyme-linked colour reaction. Infection can be detected by finding pathogen antigen or host antibodies against the pathogen.
answer_explanation: The enzyme label converts immune binding into a measurable signal.

Answer the following questions: A. Comment upon the growth status of the population on the basis of shape of the age pyramids. B. What insights can you gain about their population dynamics? Section – D
answer_text: 1950 broad-based pyramid: expanding population. 2007 inverted-bell: near-stationary/slow growth with ageing. 2050 urn-shaped: declining population. The trend shows falling birth rates, rising life expectancy, a growing elderly proportion and a shrinking workforce.
answer_explanation: Age-pyramid shape reflects relative proportions of pre-reproductive, reproductive and post-reproductive groups.

question_text: Given below is a set of information about some fruits and seeds. Fruit Fruit and seed formation P Nucellar cells surrounding the embryo sac develop into embryos. Q Ovary develops into the fruit by the application of growth hormones. R Thalamus contributes to fruit formation. S Ovary matures into a fruit after fertilisation. (2) Attempt either subpart C or D. C. Which of these fruits can be considered as parthenocarpic? Give a reason. (1) OR D. Which of the fruits P, Q, R or S is a true fruit with seeds? Give reason. (1)
answer_text: A. One embryo sac per ovule, with one egg in a monosporic embryo sac. B. It was found that the antibodies derived from colostrum (passive immunity) decreased from day 1 to 14, while the antibodies derived from immune cells (active immunity) increased between day 1 to day 1 4 and remained steady thereafter. question_text: Some plant and animal pathogens serve as one of the tools of recombinant DNA (rDNA) technology.’ A. Name one animal and one plant pathogen and discuss the pathogenic nature of both. Name an alternate method to introduce the gene of interest the pathogen would have o therwise delivered and discuss how the alternate method would deliver the gene. ii. answer_text: Agrobacterium tumefaciens (plant) uses Ti plasmid to transfer T-DNA; retroviruses infect animals and modified vectors deliver genes. rDNA enzymes include restriction endonucleases, DNA ligase, polymerases and reverse transcriptase. question_text: Justify the following statements with suitable proof/examples: - A. ‘competition is not limited to closely related species’ B. ‘competition is not always dependent on resources being limiting’ C. ‘competitive exclusion occurs in nature’ D. ‘competing species may evolve mechanisms for co-existence’ E. ‘competition in nature comes from what is called ‘competitive release’’ OR A. How does a simple food chain exemplify the First Law of Thermodynamics? B. The table below shows the number of species in different parts of the world. Name of Place Number of Bird species Columbia 1400 India 1200 Northern South America 1300 New York 105 Denmark 504 Identify the common factor in regions with a higher number of bird species and suggest at least two reasons for this greater diversity. **********
answer_text: A. Competition may occur between unrelated species, e.g., flamingoes and fish for zooplankton. B. Interference competition can occur even when resources are abundant. C. Gause's Paramecium experiments show competitive exclusion. D. Resource partitioning, as in MacArthur's warblers, permits coexistence. E. Competitive release occurs when removal of a competitor expands a species' realised niche. OR food chains obey energy conservation: energy changes form and dissipates as heat but is not created or destroyed; tropical regions have more bird species due to stable climate, high productivity and long evolutionary time.
answer_explanation: These examples show the multiple ecological forms and outcomes of competition.
